why_this_order: the one-stick order of a real machine (plans/aspire-ubuntu-one-stick.json). The stick writer and the walk-away are stand-ins here: the rig holds the order, the second look and the refusal on a stick made again, nothing of the writer or the walk-away

stages.why: the rig's stick, made by the rig's own builder (a stand-in for the stick writer)
known files in Windows before the job is written, so the product's own harvest counts them and the copy can be held to them
the default path: install beside Windows, settle-in's first start, both systems start
people forget the stick: it must not install again
the file copy (V3): settle-in's own command, then every planted file hashed where it landed; a second run must find nothing to do
the rig's install as found: a healthy drive, one disk, one account. Reclaim's check must give a plan and change nothing (the move itself needs a USB stick the rig does not have)
V15's planted fault: the Windows partition is not the one the install recorded
V15's planted fault: the drive did not report itself healthy
V15's planted fault: Windows' drive is locked, so it cannot be shown before it is deleted
V15's planted fault: another person's account is on Windows
every planted fault is put back: the check gives its plan again
back to a fresh Windows after a clean slate (the rig's stand-in)
Windows is back: the stick is made again from the same kit for the last stages
the fresh Windows gets its own scan: the job writer reads it from the stick

why_no_cancel: the owner, 2026-11-02: the last click in the window is the commit line; no countdown and no cancel after it
why_files: the file copy and reclaim's check sit after the install beside Windows and before the rollback: the copy refuses once Windows starts first again (the owner's prompt, 2026-11-17: plan them into the run order after a keep-Windows install)
